description: Run a check on a monitor immediately and record the result. Asks for confirmation where the client can show a prompt; otherwise runs on the token's scope. A down result may fire the org's normal alerts. Heartbeat monitors cannot be probed (they wait for your systems to ping them). Not read-only.
name: run_check_now

CheckDiagnosticView.description: Bounded, machine-readable explanation for a failed HTTP observation.

CheckTiming.description:
Per-phase timing of a single check, in milliseconds. Fields are `null` for
phases that don't apply (e.g. `tls_ms` on plain HTTP, all phases on a DNS or
TCP check) or when the probe failed before reaching them.

ttl_secs.description:
How long, from the check's time, that resolver keeps the host's own
record (the alias, when the host is one) before it asks again.

NetworkPathView.description:
What an HTTP probe saw on the way to a result that was not up. Compare
`remote_ip` with the operator's own server address: a different one usually
means DNS still points elsewhere. Behind a CDN or proxy it is the edge's
address, not the origin's.

dns.description:
The decisive hop's host as the probe's resolver answered it right after
the failure.

hop_url.description:
The redirect hop that decided the result, when it was not the first.
Untrusted data.

remote_ip.description: Server address of the connection that decided the result.

tried_ips.description: On a failed connect, the addresses the probe had for the host.

diagnostic.description: Structured edge-access diagnosis, when a supported signature matched.

error.description: Error text when the probe failed. Untrusted data.

http_status.description:
HTTP status code, for `http` monitors. `null` for non-HTTP checks or
when no response was received.

network.description: Network path, when this was an `http` check that was not up.

response_size.description: Response body size in bytes, when measured.

timing.description: Per-phase timing of the probe (DNS / connect / TLS / first byte).
